We argue that this shortage of prospective validation, not a shortage of computational sophistication, is the field's central constraint, and we close by identifying where methodological effort would do the most good: standardized validation reporting, tissue-resolved rather than bulk metabolic models, and closer coupling between computational prediction and the specific experimental designs capable of falsifying it.

records.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.

content.title: Operationalising digital and AI pathology in translational research and drug development: an infrastructure and regulatory perspective from biobank to companion diagnostic.
content.abstract: Digital and artificial intelligence (AI) pathology have advanced rapidly and are increasingly embedded in translational research, clinical trials and regulated diagnostic devices. Multiple reviews have addressed the underlying computational methods, oncology applications and clinical translation barriers; however, the operational and regulatory infrastructure required to deploy these technologies across the full drug-development pipeline remains under-reviewed. This structured narrative review synthesises peer-reviewed literature and regulatory documents identified through searches of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science between January 2019 and April 2026 (78 sources retained) on the end-to-end ecosystem connecting AI-ready tissue biobanks, preclinical pathology, AI-assisted patient screening, clinical-trial endpoint adjudication, central pathology review, Contract Research Organization (CRO) workflows and US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) regulatory pathways governing In Vitro Diagnostics (IVD), Software as a Medical Device (SaMD) and Companion Diagnostics (CDx). Unlike prior method-centric or oncology-clinician-centric reviews, we focus on the infrastructure between models and patients, including Laboratory Information Systems (LIS), Image Management Systems (IMS), AI orchestration and structured reporting under Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments, College of American Pathologists, Good Laboratory Practice, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice, Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and FDA frameworks. We provide a vendor-agnostic comparison of integrated pathology platforms, a mapping of FDA regulatory pathways (510(k), De Novo, premarket approval) to digital-pathology product categories, a stage-by-stage map from each drug-development challenge to its enabling infrastructure and regulatory framework, and a critical appraisal of the unresolved bottlenecks that gate broad adoption: domain shift, interpretability, annotation cost, algorithmic bias, external validation, regulatory uncertainty and reimbursement. A governed, interoperable LIS, IMS and AI ecosystem is a prerequisite for translating digital-pathology research into regulator-grade evidence. Priorities include external validation against reporting standards (Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis or Diagnosis - Artificial Intelligence (TRIPOD-AI), Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging (CLAIM), Development and Early-stage Clinical Identification and Delegation Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence (DECIDE-AI)), harmonisation with the EU AI Act and EU Medical Device Regulation and cost-effectiveness evaluation in real-world deployment.

records.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.

content.title: Artificial intelligence in emergency trauma perioperative management: applications, performance benchmarks, and translation barriers.
content.abstract: This review examines the current status of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in the perioperative management of emergency trauma. Published studies suggest performance advantages of AI over traditional methods in prehospital triage, radiographic injury detection, massive transfusion prediction, and early warning of postoperative complications, although findings vary across study designs and validation settings. However, actual adoption in trauma care remains limited due to data heterogeneity, performance degradation in external validation, workflow integration challenges, lack of interpretability, and a scarcity of prospective interventional evidence. This review further argues that methodologically inflated benchmark performance constitutes an underrecognized barrier to adoption in its own right, and that bridging the implementation gap will likely require a shift from area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)-centered reporting toward reporting sensitivity at prespecified clinical thresholds and evaluating patient outcomes in prospective interventional trials.

records.title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research.
records.publisher: The Indian journal of radiology & imaging

content.title: Legal and Regulatory Considerations for Artificial Intelligence Use in Medical and Radiology Research.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into medical imaging and radiology research, improving image acquisition, interpretation, workflow efficiency, and decision support. However, its rapid adoption has introduced complex legal and regulatory challenges involving patient privacy, data governance, algorithm validation, liability, intellectual property, transparency, cybersecurity, and ethical oversight. A comprehensive understanding of the evolving legal landscape is essential for the safe, effective, and legally compliant implementation of AI in radiology.

Methods

A narrative review of the published literature and current regulatory guidance was conducted. Relevant international legal and regulatory frameworks governing AI in medical imaging were evaluated, including the European Union Artificial Intelligence Act, General Data Protection Regulation, U.S. Food and Drug Administration guidance on Software as a Medical Device (SaMD), Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act, World Health Organization recommendations, International Medical Device Regulators Forum principles, and selected national regulations. Key topics reviewed included data protection, informed consent, AI validation, regulatory approval pathways, post-market surveillance, cybersecurity, algorithmic bias, explainability, and medico-legal responsibility.

Results

Current regulatory frameworks increasingly classify AI-enabled radiology software as SaMD, requiring risk-based evaluation, clinical validation, quality management systems, and continuous post-market performance monitoring. Regulatory authorities emphasize transparency, human oversight, data security, and lifecycle governance of AI systems. Nevertheless, important legal challenges remain, including liability for AI-assisted diagnostic errors, ownership of AI-generated outputs, secondary use of imaging data, cross-border data sharing, algorithmic bias, and regulation of adaptive or continuously learning AI models.

Conclusions

The legal framework governing AI in radiology is evolving in parallel with technological innovation. Responsible integration of AI into clinical practice and research requires harmonized international regulations, robust data governance, standardized validation protocols, transparent algorithm development, and clearly defined legal accountability. Continued collaboration among radiologists, researchers, regulators, policymakers, industry, and legal experts will be essential to ensure that AI technologies remain safe, ethical, equitable, and trustworthy while maximizing their potential to improve patient care.

records.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
records.publisher: MedEdPORTAL : the journal of teaching and learning resources

content.title: A Case-Based Framework for Teaching Artificial Intelligence Applications in Medical Education.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML)-based tools are emerging across many areas of medicine. The next generation of medical professionals must be prepared to critically assess the tools they will use, including how they work and the ethical or legal implications of their implementation. To address this need, we developed a generalizable case-writing framework that enables educators and learners to engage with clinical cases integrating AI/ML concepts, clinical reasoning, and ethical considerations.

Methods

We designed a case-writing template to compose clinical case scenarios that integrate clinical, technical, and ethical/legal learning objectives relating to AI applications in medicine. Medical students used this template to construct 3 cases. Student-authored cases were presented to a broader audience in 1-hour sessions: first as a pilot event, then as a class-wide lecture for 140 fourth-year medical students in a transition-into-residency course.

Results

After the sessions, student audiences had a statistically significant increase in familiarity with key AI terminology, a greater appreciation for the importance of ethical considerations of AI applications in health care, and an increased perceived importance of integrating AI-related topics into the medical curriculum.

Discussion

A case-based framework provides a scalable approach to integrating AI education into existing curricula by connecting clinical scenarios with technical concepts and the ethical considerations of AI adoption; cases offer a familiar format that helps learners understand AI applications in patient care while exploring implementation challenges. The case-writing template and 3 sample cases are provided as adaptable resources for educators seeking to incorporate AI literacy.

records.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
records.publisher: European spine journal : official publication of the European Spine Society, the European Spinal Deformity Society, and the European Section of the Cervical Spine Research Society

content.title: Integrating predictive modeling, imaging, and EHR-linked decision support in spine informatics.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly transforming spine care by enabling analysis of imaging, clinical, and textual data to support diagnosis, risk stratification, and treatment planning. Techniques including deep learning-based image analysis, radiomics, and natural language processing (NLP) offer opportunities to standardize interpretation and derive quantitative biomarkers beyond human visual assessment. This narrative review examines recent innovations in spine-focused biomedical informatics and evaluates their clinical relevance and translational challenges.

Methods

A narrative review was conducted, focusing on AI in spine care across imaging, radiomics, NLP of electronic health records, and clinical decision support. Literature was selected via targeted PubMed searches; studies describing technical development, validation, and clinical implementation were synthesized, addressing explainability, uncertainty, workflow, and regulation.

Results

Convolutional neural networks enable vertebral and disc segmentation, detection of degenerative and traumatic pathology, and quantitative assessment of paraspinal musculature. Radiomics approaches extract high-dimensional imaging features that improve the prediction of osteoporosis, fracture risk, tumor characterization, and surgical outcomes. NLP techniques, including emerging large language models, unlock clinically relevant information from unstructured text, enhancing outcome prediction and population-level analyses. Multimodal clinical decision support systems integrating imaging, EHR data, and NLP-derived features demonstrate promise for personalized risk assessment and treatment guidance. Challenges remain regarding data heterogeneity, generalizability, privacy, and prospective validation.

Conclusion

AI-driven biomedical informatics holds substantial promise to enhance diagnostic accuracy, prognostication, and personalized decision-making in spine care. Successful clinical translation will require robust validation, explainable, uncertainty-aware models, regulatory alignment, and integration into clinical workflows to ensure safe, trustworthy, and patient-centered adoption.

records.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.

content.title: Experimental Protocols for Developing and Validating Explainable AI Models in Secure Healthcare Diagnostics.
content.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI) has drastically enhanced healthcare diagnostics with automated disease detection, predictive analytics, and intelligent systems for clinical decision support. Nevertheless, the black-box nature of deep learning models hampers interpretability, clinical trust, and regulatory acceptance and raises concerns about data privacy and cybersecurity. This paper presents comprehensive experimental frameworks for developing and evaluating explainable AI models for secure healthcare diagnostics. The suggested model combines responsible data management, multimodal preprocessing, secure deep learning models, explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods, and reproducible validation procedures in a single healthcare diagnostic pipeline. Methods of explaining, such as Grad-CAM, SHAP, LIME, and counterfactual analysis, were used to make the models more transparent and understandable for clinicians. At the same time, federated learning and differential privacy methods were used to securely manage highly sensitive patient data. Experimental evaluation has shown 96% classification accuracy, 94% sensitivity, and 95% specificity. These results were consistent in heterogeneous healthcare datasets. Compared to traditional black-box models, the explainability framework not only enhanced the interpretability of the results but also more accurately identified the regions relevant for diagnosis. Moreover, the secure federated learning architecture minimized privacy leakages without sacrificing the predictive performance and remained robust even when exposed to adversarial perturbations. An external evaluation also confirmed the reproducibility and generalizability of the protocols involved. This methodology offers a comprehensive and reliable foundation for deploying AI-powered diagnostics across multiple healthcare domains: radiology, pathology, oncology, cardiology, neurology, and precision medicine.

records.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.

content.title: Beyond Accuracy: Validation, Reproducibility, and Deployment Readiness of AI in Food Safety and Quality.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly proposed for detecting microbial and chemical hazards in food, but laboratory accuracies are rarely reproduced in routine use. This structured narrative review examined whether reported performance is traceable, independently validated, and transferable to operational settings. Eight bibliographic databases and seven institutional routes were searched for English-language records published from January 2018 to May 2026, and we screened the records; the final corpus comprised 76 sources (53 journal articles, 9 conference papers, 2 preprints, and 12 institutional or regulatory documents). Seven primary studies supporting the quantitative evidence were appraised individually against 11 indicators, including test-set independence, external validation, and leakage control. Physical-hazard inspection and narrow-matrix spectral grading had the strongest deployment evidence, whereas microbial and chemical screening remained at laboratory or pilot scale. Among the appraised studies, the most credible estimates came from physically or temporally independent test sets, and no sensor-based study evaluated transfer to another instrument or laboratory. Deep learning showed clear advantages for image-based tasks but not consistently for small-sample spectral calibration. Adoption is limited mainly by validation design, recalibration burden, false-alarm costs, and the absence of a regulatory pathway rather than by accuracy. AI is best positioned as a screening and decision-support layer linked to confirmatory testing and human oversight.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence for Early Cancer Detection in Nigeria: A Contextual Narrative Review of Applications, Barriers, and Implementation Pathways.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence for Early Cancer Detection in Nigeria: A Contextual Narrative Review of Applications, Barriers, and Implementation Pathways.
content.abstract:
Background and aims

Cancer remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with late-stage diagnosis driving high mortality. While artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated strong diagnostic performance globally, its role in Nigeria's oncology landscape is poorly defined. This review synthesizes current evidence on AI applications for early cancer detection in Nigeria, critically evaluates methodological and infrastructural barriers, and proposes context-specific implementation pathways.

Methods

A narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and African Journals Online to identify literature published from 2014 to 2024.

Results

Sixty studies met the inclusion criteria, of which 15 were Nigeria-led. AI models achieved high diagnostic accuracy in breast (91%-98%), cervical (92%-96%), and prostate cancers (Area Under the Curve: 0.93-0.97). Smartphone-based AI pilots in Lagos and Ibadan demonstrated feasibility in low-resource settings. However, methodological heterogeneity, limited local datasets, and the absence of standardized benchmarks constrain generalizability. Key barriers include unreliable electricity, poor broadband, workforce shortages, and weak regulatory frameworks.

Conclusion

AI offers transformative potential for early cancer detection in Nigeria, but success requires staged implementation: short-term pilots in teaching hospitals, medium-term development of national AI guidelines and workforce training, and long-term integration into cancer control plans. Investment in local data repositories, renewable-energy-powered diagnostic centers, and structured public-private partnerships is essential to reduce diagnostic delays and mortality.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence in Diabetes Mellitus Management: A Narrative Review of Advances, Architectures, and Translational Challenges.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence in Diabetes Mellitus Management: A Narrative Review of Advances, Architectures, and Translational Challenges.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Diabetes Mellitus (DM), a chronic disorder caused by insulin deficiency, dysfunction, or both, is projected to affect 640 million people by 2040. Traditional management is limited by drug resistance, poor adherence, and insufficient personalization. This review examines Artificial Intelligence (AI) applications addressing these gaps in DM care.

Methods

PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and Google Scholar were searched (January 2020-December 2025) using combinations of diabetes mellitus, artificial intelligence, machine learning, deep learning, federated learning, explainable AI, and blockchain. Studies addressing AI-based risk prediction, glucose forecasting, complication detection, and secure or transparent frameworks were included, reported by diabetes subtype where relevant.

Results

Convolutional neural networks, long short-term memory networks, support vector machines, and transformer architectures have improved glucose forecasting, complication screening, and risk prediction. Federated learning enables privacy-preserving multi-institutional training, while SHAP and LIME improve interpretability, and blockchain offers a tamper-proof audit layer. However, most high-performing models remain internally validated, limiting generalizability.

Discussion

Unlike prior reviews that address a single application domain or treat T1DM and T2DM as a single population, this review is organized around their distinct AI design needs and classifies applications as experimental, commercial, or regulator-approved. AI can extend beyond technical accuracy by integrating diverse clinical data, though explainability and validation remain central to adoption.

Conclusion

AI has the potential to transform DM care through more precise forecasting, earlier complication detection, and individualized treatment. Realizing this requires stronger regulatory frameworks, external validation, reduced demographic bias, and improved interpretability, prioritized through prospective multicenter studies, standardized datasets, and explainability standards embedded in clinical workflows.

records.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.

content.title: AI-Enabled Animal Behavior Analysis for Translational Pharmacology and Therapeutic Discovery.
content.abstract: Animal behavior is a critical endpoint in preclinical pharmacology, toxicology, and therapeutic discovery, yet conventional behavioral scoring remains labor-intensive, low-dimensional, and difficult to reproduce across laboratories. Artificial intelligence (AI) can now quantify behavior from video with greater spatial, temporal, and phenotypic resolution. This review summarizes how object detection, markerless pose estimation, unsupervised behavioral segmentation, foundation models, and autonomous analysis agents are reshaping behavioral phenotyping. General-purpose object detectors rapidly localize and track animals, whereas open-source pose-estimation tools extend measurement beyond centroid tracking to body-part trajectories and fine motor patterns; paired with supervised classifiers, they have matched human scoring and exceeded some commercial systems. Technical accuracy alone does not establish behavioral construct validity or pharmacological validity. Unsupervised methods such as Motion Sequencing represent drug responses and disease-model phenotypes as structured changes in behavioral states rather than only as predefined endpoints, providing high-dimensional fingerprints of pharmacological action. Segmentation and tracking foundation models may reduce annotation burden but require validation across species, strain, sex, apparatus, and paradigm. AI agents may assist with literature review, code generation, analysis auditing, and figure production but must remain within transparent, human-supervised workflows. In behavioral pharmacology, pose estimation is established as a measurement method and emerging as a drug-effect endpoint, supervised classification and unsupervised segmentation are emerging, and foundation models and agents remain prospective. AI-enabled behavioral analysis can become a reproducible phenotyping layer for drug discovery and toxicology if researchers adopt open pipelines, rigorous validation, and reporting standards, rather than replacing one opaque measurement system with another.

records.title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review.

content.title: Augmentation or erosion? Artificial intelligence and the transformation of clinical reasoning: a critical narrative review.
content.abstract:
Background

Artificial intelligence (AI) systems are used to support diagnosis, but a model's accuracy does not establish that clinicians reason more accurately when they use it. This review appraises how AI decision support and large language models affect physicians' diagnostic performance and the risks of relying on them.

Methods

This critical narrative review follows the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles. Scopus, PubMed/MEDLINE, SciELO and LILACS were searched in July and August 2026 in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Eligible studies, published from 2015 onward, compared AI-assisted with unassisted clinicians, measured reliance on AI or unassisted performance after exposure to it, or externally validated deployed models. A single author selected sources purposively. Nine primary studies were appraised with an adapted Critical Appraisal Skills Programme framework.

Results

In randomized trials of perceptual tasks, AI support improved detection. In the MASAI mammography screening trial, cancer detection rose from 5.0 to 6.4 per 1,000 women, reading workload fell by 44%, and the interval-cancer rate was non-inferior. In colonoscopy, computer-aided detection raised the adenoma detection rate from 40.4% to 54.8%. In the only randomized trial of open-ended diagnostic reasoning, access to GPT-4 did not improve physicians' scores (76% vs. 74%; P=.60 ), although the model alone scored 92%. Evidence of harm came from smaller or non-randomized studies: reader accuracy fell sharply when AI suggestions were incorrect or the AI missed a cancer; physicians trained in AI literacy were still misled by erroneous model advice; unassisted adenoma detection fell from 28.4% to 22.4% after routine AI use in one pre-post study; and a deployed sepsis model discriminated poorly on external validation (area under the curve 0.63). No eligible study from Latin America was identified.

Conclusions

In the studies reviewed, AI assistance improved clinician performance in bounded detection tasks but not in open-ended diagnostic reasoning, where evidence is limited to one vignette-based trial. The evidence that reliance on AI can impair performance comes from single or design-limited studies and does not establish how large or lasting such effects are. Benefit therefore cannot be inferred from model accuracy alone; assisted and unassisted clinician performance should be measured directly.

records.title: Artificial intelligence-based voice biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of neurological diseases: current evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.

content.title: Artificial intelligence-based voice biomarkers for early detection and monitoring of neurological diseases: current evidence, limitations, and clinical perspectives.
content.abstract:
Background

Early diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring of neurological diseases remain major clinical challenges because current diagnostic approaches are often expensive, invasive, or insufficiently sensitive to detect early functional changes. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as a promising approach for analyzing voice and speech as non-invasive digital biomarkers capable of capturing subtle alterations associated with neurological dysfunction.

Methods

This narrative review analyzed studies published between 2015 and 2026 retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. The review critically examines the limitations of current neurological diagnostic methods, summarizes the available evidence on AI-based voice and speech biomarkers, discusses machine learning and deep learning approaches applied to speech analysis, and evaluates the methodological, ethical, and regulatory challenges that currently limit their clinical implementation.

Results

Current evidence indicates that AI-based voice biomarkers have considerable potential for screening, diagnostic support, and longitudinal monitoring of neurological disorders, including Parkinson's disease, Alzheimer's disease, multiple sclerosis, and other neurodegenerative conditions. Several studies report high diagnostic performance under controlled experimental settings. However, substantial heterogeneity in study design, sample size, languages, speech acquisition protocols, validation strategies, and reporting standards limits direct comparison between studies and hinders clinical translation. External validation and prospective multicenter studies remain scarce.

Conclusion

AI-based voice analysis represents a promising, scalable, and non-invasive complement to conventional neurological assessment, with particular potential for remote screening and disease monitoring. Nevertheless, current evidence does not yet support routine clinical implementation. Future progress will depend on standardized speech acquisition protocols, robust external validation across diverse populations, explainable AI models, and regulatory frameworks capable of ensuring safety, reproducibility, and clinical reliability.

records.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
records.publisher: Journal of basic and clinical physiology and pharmacology

content.title: Clinical integration of artificial intelligence for diagnosis, risk prediction and management of rare cardiovascular diseases.
content.abstract:
Introduction

RCDs comprise a diverse group of inherited and acquired disorders characterized by low prevalence, substantial genetic and phenotypic heterogeneity, delayed diagnosis, and limited evidence-based therapeutic options. These challenges contribute to poor clinical outcomes, including progressive heart failure, malignant arrhythmias, and sudden cardiac death.

Content

This review summarizes recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) for the diagnosis and management of RCDs. AI technologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and multimodal data integration, enable comprehensive analysis of electrocardiography, echocardiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, computed tomography, genomic and multi-omics data, biomarkers, wearable devices, and electronic health records. These approaches improve early disease detection, phenotypic classification, risk stratification, prognostic prediction and personalized treatment planning.

Summary

Current evidence suggests that AI significantly enhances diagnostic accuracy, prognostic assessment, and individualized clinical decision-making in patients with RCDs.

Outlook

Future clinical implementation requires standardized multicenter datasets, prospective validation, transparent and explainable algorithms, robust regulatory and ethical frameworks, and seamless integration into healthcare systems. Continued interdisciplinary collaboration will accelerate AI-driven precision cardiovascular medicine and improve outcomes for patients with rare cardiovascular diseases.

records.title: Growth, Specialty Distribution, and Regulatory Pathways of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices Authorized in the United States From 1995 to 2026: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.

content.title: Growth, Specialty Distribution, and Regulatory Pathways of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Medical Devices Authorized in the United States From 1995 to 2026: A Cross-Sectional Analysis.
content.abstract: Introduction The United States Food and Drug Administration (FDA) publishes a list of artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled medical devices authorized for marketing. Annual authorizations have risen sharply in recent years, and an updated analysis of the complete list is needed. This study aimed to characterize regulatory authorizations on the full list through mid-2026. Methods A cross-sectional analysis of all 1,614 entries on the FDA AI-Enabled Medical Device List (final decisions from September 1995 to June 2026) was performed. Regulatory pathway, year, lead review panel, product code, and manufacturer group were derived for each entry. Growth was estimated by log-linear regression, trends were tested with the Cochran-Armitage test and logistic regression with manufacturer-clustered standard errors, and associations were tested with chi-squared and Fisher exact tests, with Holm adjustment for multiple testing. Results Annual authorizations rose from 18 in 2016 to 335 in 2025, an estimated growth of 35.3% per year (95% confidence interval (CI) 27.0-44.3), and 977 of 1,614 entries (60.5%) were authorized from 2023 onward. Radiology accounted for 1,230 entries (76.2%); its share peaked at 347 of 405 (85.7%) in 2020-2022 and fell to 750 of 977 (76.8%) in 2023-2026 (p < 0.001), while radiology authorizations kept growing in absolute terms and the number of represented specialty panels rose from 10 to 16. The 510(k) pathway accounted for 1,553 authorizations (96.2%), and radiology entries were less likely than others to use the De Novo or premarket approval pathways (18 of 1,230, 1.5% vs. 43 of 384, 11.2%; odds ratio 0.14, 95% CI 0.08-0.27 after adjustment for era). Of 40 De Novo grants, 22 created product codes that later received 181 510(k) clearances. Imaging systems such as ultrasound, computed tomography, and magnetic resonance scanners accounted for 399 entries (24.7%), and seven large manufacturers accounted for 288 of these (72.2%). Findings were similar for 1,195 deduplicated devices and for entries through December 2025. Conclusions FDA authorization of AI-enabled devices continues to accelerate. Radiology remains dominant and still growing, while other specialties are expanding alongside it; the 510(k) pathway predominates, and a growing share of authorizations concerns AI embedded in imaging equipment. These findings describe regulatory authorizations rather than clinical adoption, and they identify transparency about AI functions in conventional devices and AI-specific post-market surveillance as topics for further study.

records.title: Synergizing New Approach Methodologies and Artificial Intelligence: Charting the Paradigm Shift Toward Next-Generation Chemical Risk Assessment.

content.title: Synergizing New Approach Methodologies and Artificial Intelligence: Charting the Paradigm Shift Toward Next-Generation Chemical Risk Assessment.
content.abstract: The escalating global chemical inventory, coupled with the ethical and scientific inadequacies of traditional animal testing, has made a change in approach unavoidable in chemical risk assessment. This review examines how the combined use of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping this field. NAMs-including micro physiological systems, high-content screening, multi-omics, and in silico tools-generate high-dimensional and mechanism-anchored data. Concurrently, AI, spanning advanced machine learning and generative models, serves as the essential integrative engine that converts this data into actionable toxicological insight. We present a framework delineating how these two streams of technology interact to operationalize Next-Generation Risk Assessment (NGRA) across its entire pipeline-from intelligent hazard identification and refined exposure prediction to dynamic, population-aware risk characterization. The evidence indicates a shift from empirical, observation-based toxicology toward a predictive, mechanism-centric, and personalized science. By mapping specific AI techniques to core NAMs data streams and NGRA decision points across the hazard, exposure, and risk characterization continuum, this review provides a coherent roadmap for regulators, researchers, and industry stakeholders. We also consider environmental applications, including complex mixtures, persistent organic pollutants (POPs), per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), and emerging contaminants, while noting that the supporting evidence is more limited than for human health endpoints. Finally, we critically examine remaining challenges and chart forward-looking paths, including the development of chemical "digital twins," causal AI models, and real-time risk warning systems. We argue that progress depends on integrating NAMs and AI within a more efficient, ethical, and protective global chemical safety framework. However, barriers remain, including limited reproducibility across chemical domains, inadequate external validation, the hallucination risk of large language models in regulatory contexts, and the gap between academic development and regulatory acceptance. Open data infrastructure, standardized benchmarking, and harmonized validation frameworks will be essential to realize the full potential of this approach.

records.title: Synthetic artificial intelligence in cardiology: from generative models to clinical applications.

content.title: Synthetic artificial intelligence in cardiology: from generative models to clinical applications.
content.abstract: Synthetic artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly redefining biomedical research-yet in cardiovascular medicine, its clinical relevance remains obscure, underexplored, and underestimated. Unlike traditional AI, which interprets data, synthetic AI generates entirely new, patient-like information: from realistic ECG signals to cardiac imaging and virtual cohorts that simulate disease progression. While recent publications have addressed specific synthetic AI tools in cardiology, no prior review has comprehensively synthesized their architectures, clinical applications, and implementation challenges within a single, practice-oriented framework. This State-of-the-Art Review fills that gap. We provide a clear, critical synthesis of core architectures-Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), Diffusion Models, Transformers, Autoregressive Models, Digital Twins, and Synthetic Cohort Simulators-and map their emerging cardiovascular applications. We examine technical barriers, ethical concerns, regulatory uncertainties, and integration challenges, while anchoring the discussion in real-world clinical priorities. This review is not only a scientific analysis-it is a call to engagement. For academic researchers, it offers conceptual and technical clarity. For clinicians in resource-constrained settings, it presents synthetic AI not as abstract innovation, but as a practical opportunity to enhance diagnostic precision, optimize workflows, and extend clinical insight. Traditional AI supports cardiologists by interpreting data; synthetic AI extends this paradigm by creating new, clinically coherent information that enhances decision-making without replacing physician expertise. As investment grows and methods mature, cardiologists must shape this evolution-not as passive adopters, but as active drivers. This review invites them to take the wheel.

records.title: Exploring the potential of artificial intelligence and machine learning in orthopaedic surgery.
records.publisher: Bulletin of the Hospital for Joint Disease (2013)

content.title: Exploring the potential of artificial intelligence and machine learning in orthopaedic surgery.
content.abstract:
Abstract

Artificial intelligence (AI) has emerged as one of the most transformative technological forces in modern medicine, with rapidly expanding applications throughout medicine including orthopaedic surgery. Recent advances in machine learning, deep learning, and natural language processing have accelerated the development of AI-enabled tools with direct relevance to orthopaedic practice. This review provides a basic overview of how AI works and current uses of AI in medicine and orthopaedics across multiple domains including documentation efficiency, patient communication, operating room optimization, imaging analysis, rehabilitation, education, and research, and briefly describes AI's limitations, ethical and legal concerns, and cost. These applications are all already being used in orthopaedics or have clear direct translation. AI holds considerable potential to augment orthopaedic care by streamlining workflows, enhancing decision-making, and improving patient outcomes. However, responsible integration requires rigorous validation, transparency, clinician oversight, and ongoing education. As AI adoption accelerates, orthopaedic surgeons must critically evaluate emerging technologies to ensure that.

records.title: Acidic cannabinoids in brain disorders: Neurobiological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges.

content.title: Acidic cannabinoids in brain disorders: Neurobiological mechanisms, preclinical evidence, and translational challenges.
content.abstract: Acidic cannabinoids, including tetrahydrocannabinolic acid (THCA), cannabidiolic acid (CBDA), cannabigerolic acid (CBGA), and related biosynthetic precursors, represent the predominant phytocannabinoid forms naturally produced by Cannabis sativa. Long considered pharmacologically inactive intermediates, these compounds are now increasingly recognized as bioactive molecules with potential therapeutic relevance for brain disorders. Compared with their decarboxylated counterparts, acidic cannabinoids exhibit distinct physicochemical, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic properties that may confer reduced psychotropic liability together with unique neurobiological effects. Emerging preclinical evidence indicates that acidic cannabinoids modulate multiple processes implicated in neurological and psychiatric disorders, including serotonergic and endocannabinoid signaling, neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, calcium dyshomeostasis, and synaptic transmission. In this review, we critically examine current knowledge regarding acidic cannabinoids in the context of brain disorders. We first summarize their biosynthesis, chemical stability, pharmacokinetic characteristics, and pharmacological differences from neutral cannabinoids. We then examine preclinical evidence supporting their potential therapeutic effects in epilepsy, anxiety, depression, psychosis-related conditions, and neurodegenerative diseases, including Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, Huntington's disease, and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. We also discuss how artificial intelligence and computational approaches may support target identification, formulation optimization, pharmacokinetic modeling, and the development of personalized cannabinoid-based interventions. Finally, we highlight key methodological and translational challenges limiting the field and outline priorities for future research. Overall, acidic cannabinoids emerge as promising but still underexplored multitarget compounds with potential relevance for the treatment of brain disorders.

records.title: Advancing multi-scale plant phenotyping for precision agriculture and sustainable crop production.
records.publisher: Journal of Zhejiang University. Science. B

content.title: Advancing multi-scale plant phenotyping for precision agriculture and sustainable crop production.
content.abstract: Plant phenotyping captures the integrated structural and functional traits of crops across cellular, tissue, organ, whole-plant, and population scales. It represents the outward expression of genotype-environment interactions and provides essential technological support for precision breeding, smart agriculture, and sustainable crop production. As farming shifts from experience-based to data-driven decision-making, the efficient acquisition and integrated analysis of phenotypic information at multiple spatial scales has emerged as a major research frontier at the intersection of agronomy, plant science, and agricultural engineering.

records.title: Comparative effectiveness of various exercise modalities on arterial stiffness and endothelial function in older adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

content.title: Comparative effectiveness of various exercise modalities on arterial stiffness and endothelial function in older adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Objective

We aimed to evaluate the comparative modulatory efficacy of various exercise modalities on endothelial function and arterial stiffness in older adults via a systematic review and network meta-analysis.

Methods

We systematically searched eight electronic databases to identify randomised controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating seven distinct exercise modalities (aerobic, walking, resistance, combined, mind-body, stretching, and whole-body vibration training) in older adults aged 60 years or older. Eligibility criteria stipulated supervised, standardised training programmes with a minimum duration of 4 weeks and continuous monitoring of exercise intensity. To comprehensively evaluate the comparative efficacy of these modalities on arterial stiffness and endothelial function, a frequentist network meta-analysis was performed to mathematically integrate direct and indirect trial evidence. The certainty and quality of evidence were rigorously assessed via the Cochrane RoB 2.0 and CINeMA frameworks.

Results

In primary analyses, whole-body vibration and resistance training ranked highest for enhancing endothelial function (FMD), whereas aerobic training and walking were associated with greater improvements in attenuating arterial stiffness (baPWV); However, extensive confidence interval overlap precluded definitive claims of clinical superiority. Regarding secondary outcomes, stretching exercise showed a higher probability of reducing systolic blood pressure (SBP) based on mean ranking estimates, while combined training ranked among the leading modalities for lowering diastolic blood pressure (DBP), though these findings warrant cautious interpretation as head-to-head differences generally lacked statistical significance. The observed reductions in blood pressure, particularly systolic decreases exceeding 10 mmHg, carry substantial clinical relevance, given that a reduction of this magnitude is typically associated with an approximate 20% down-risk in major adverse cardiovascular events within older populations. According to the CINeMA framework, the certainty of evidence was graded as moderate-to-high for FMD outcomes, but low-to-moderate for arterial stiffness comparisons.

Conclusion

Accumulating evidence suggests that exercise-induced vascular adaptations in older adults are likely modality-specific. Whole-body vibration and resistance training appear to confer substantial optimisation upon endothelial function, whereas aerobic training and walking demonstrate potential advantages in attenuating arterial stiffness. Rather than supporting an immediate paradigm shift, these findings suggest that integrating exercise monitoring tailored to specific phenotypic characteristics may refine clinical prescriptions, though such implementation should be interpreted with caution given inherent study heterogeneity, reliance on indirect network comparisons, and potential risks of bias.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251236872, identifier CRD420251236872.

records.title: Nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors for traumatic brain injury biomarker detection: a review of analytical performance, machine learning integration, clinical validation, and point-of-care translation.

content.title: Nanomaterial-enhanced biosensors for traumatic brain injury biomarker detection: a review of analytical performance, machine learning integration, clinical validation, and point-of-care translation.
content.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) affects an estimated 69 million people each year and remains difficult to diagnose rapidly because conventional assessment relies heavily on neurological examination and computed tomography, which may miss subtle injuries or be unavailable in many clinical settings. Blood-based biomarkers, including S100B, glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP), ubiquitin carboxy-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCH-L1), and neurofilament light chain (NfL), provide measurable indicators of glial, neuronal, and axonal injury across different stages of TBI. Nanomaterial-based biosensors have emerged as promising platforms for detecting these biomarkers with high sensitivity, rapid response, and potential for point-of-care testing. This review evaluates recent advances in electrochemical, optical, and emerging biosensor technologies for TBI biomarker detection, with emphasis on analytical performance, clinical validation, and translational potential. The review examines the contributions of gold nanoparticles, graphene derivatives, carbon nanotubes, MXenes, and related nanomaterials to improving signal transduction, surface functionalization, and detection sensitivity in immunosensors and aptasensors. Key analytical parameters, including limit of detection, linear dynamic range, assay time, and selectivity, are assessed against clinically relevant thresholds such as the FDA-cleared GFAP cutoff of 22 pg./mL and the UCH-L1 cutoff of 327 pg./mL. Progress in multiplex biosensing, artificial intelligence-assisted data analysis, and portable diagnostic platforms is also discussed. Although many nanomaterial-enabled biosensors achieve analytical performance well below clinical detection thresholds, most have been validated only in buffer solutions or spiked biological samples, with limited evaluation in patient cohorts. Future progress will depend on robust clinical validation, standardized performance assessment, scalable manufacturing, and regulatory alignment to support the translation of TBI biosensors into routine point-of-care practice.

records.title: Bridging the vaccine gap: Scientific and technological advances for diseases lacking effective vaccines.

content.title: Bridging the vaccine gap: Scientific and technological advances for diseases lacking effective vaccines.
content.abstract: Despite remarkable achievements in infectious disease control, more than 20 major pathogens responsible for significant global morbidity and mortality remain without licensed, effective vaccines. This so-called 'vaccine gap' disproportionately burdens low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), exacerbating health inequities and threatening global pandemic preparedness. This review comprehensively examines scientific and technological advances that are actively bridging the vaccine gap, with emphasis on novel platform technologies, immunological innovations, and translational strategies. We conducted a systematic narrative review of literature published between 2015 and 2024, encompassing peer-reviewed articles, WHO reports, clinical trial registries, and regulatory agency databases. Six transformative technology clusters were identified: (1) mRNA and self-amplifying RNA (saRNA) platforms enabling rapid antigen production; (2) viral-vectored vaccines with improved immune breadth; (3) structure-guided antigen design using cryo-electron microscopy and artificial intelligence (AI)-driven protein engineering; (4) broadly neutralising monoclonal antibodies as surrogate vaccine benchmarks; (5) mucosal and inhalable delivery systems targeting tissue-resident immunity; and (6) combination adjuvant systems amplifying magnitude and durability of protective responses. Clinical translation is exemplified by candidates against HIV-1, tuberculosis (TB), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in infants, and Plasmodium falciparum malaria. Convergence of AI-assisted rational antigen design, next-generation mRNA platforms, and innovative adjuvant-delivery pairings represents a paradigm shift toward vaccinatable diseases previously considered intractable. Equitable access frameworks and regulatory harmonisation across LMICs remain critical unresolved challenges.

records.title: Applications of Federated Large Language Model for Adverse Drug Reactions Prediction: Scoping Review.

content.title: Applications of Federated Large Language Model for Adverse Drug Reactions Prediction: Scoping Review.
content.abstract:
Background

Adverse drug reactions (ADR) present significant challenges in health care, where early prevention is vital for effective treatment and patient safety. Traditional supervised learning methods struggle to address heterogeneous health care data due to their unstructured nature, regulatory constraints, and restricted access to sensitive personal identifiable information.

Objective

This review aims to explore the potential of federated learning (FL) combined with natural language processing and large language models (LLMs) to enhance ADR prediction. FL enables decentralized training across client clusters with limited resources, while LLMs effectively process unstructured health care data. By aggregating client-trained models into a global model, FL ensures broader data inclusion while maintaining privacy.

Methods

A scoping review was conducted on peer-reviewed publications retrieved from Google Scholar and Semantic Scholar between 2019 and 2024.

Results

Following the PRISMA (Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses) protocol, 145 articles from PubMed, arXiv, IEEE, and ACL Anthology met the inclusion criteria. Of these, 12 articles were selected for an in-depth review to examine use cases in ADR prediction. We synthesized ADR data sources on structured and unstructured data types, use cases of FL integrated with natural language processing, and open-source frameworks for ADR identifications and predictions. Special attention is given to unstructured ADR prediction using federated learning with large language models, including development and deployment strategies and evaluation metrics.

Conclusions

Given the recent emergence of LLM, the integration of FL and LLM for ADR prediction remains in its early stage, with limited documented use cases. This review explored the potential applications and highlighted the advancements of federated learning with large language models in health care research, particularly in ADR prediction. Key focus areas include fine-tuning and merging algorithms, fairness and unbiasedness, implementation challenges, and real-world deployment strategies. By synthesizing current insights, this review aims to lay the groundwork for future research in privacy-preserving and scalable ADR prediction systems.

records.title: Current challenges for global equity related to the implementation of artificial intelligence in pediatric imaging.

content.title: Current challenges for global equity related to the implementation of artificial intelligence in pediatric imaging.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming medical imaging, offering unprecedented opportunities to enhance diagnostic accuracy, streamline workflows, and personalize care. However, its integration into pediatric radiology presents unique challenges that threaten to widen existing global health disparities if not addressed thoughtfully. These challenges are related to data inequality and bias in model development, infrastructure disparities, regulatory and ethical gaps, workforce capacity and training gaps, language and localization barriers, costs and commercialization, and sustainability and long-term support issues. This article, written by representatives from the World Federation of Pediatric Imaging (WFPI), will address the key barriers to global validation and implementation of AI in pediatric radiology and how they can be addressed. By linking these domains to practical actions and responsibilities and outlining a time-sequenced roadmap, this paper provides an equity-focused, pediatric-specific framework to guide global implementation.

records.title: Efficacy and safety of Lanqin Oral Liquid combined with Western medicine for the treatment of pharyngitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy and safety of Lanqin Oral Liquid combined with Western medicine for the treatment of pharyngitis: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

This study aimed to systematically review and meta-analyze the efficacy and safety of Lanqin Oral Liquid combined with Western medicine for the treatment of pharyngitis.

Methods

A comprehensive and systematic literature search was conducted by two independent reviewers across six electronic databases-PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, WanFang and VIP. Outcomes included the effective rate, symptoms improvement, C-reactive protein (CRP) levels, and the incidence of adverse events. The Cochrane Risk of Bias tool was adopted to evaluate the quality of the included studies, and RevMan 5.4 and Stata 15.0 software were used for meta-analysis.

Results

A total of 12 studies were included. The effective rate of Lanqin Oral Liquid combined with Western medicine for pharyngitis was significantly higher than that of Western medicine monotherapy (OR = 3.68, 95% CI [2.55, 5.33], Z = 6.92, P < 0.001), with no heterogeneity across studies (I2 = 0%, P = 0.73). Compared with Western medicine monotherapy, combination therapy significantly shortened the disappearance time of pharyngeal redness/swelling, sore throat, and phlegm in patients with acute pharyngitis, and reduced Reflux Symptom Index score and Reflux Finding Score in those with chronic pharyngitis (all P < 0.05). The combination therapy was significantly superior to Western medicine monotherapy in reducing CRP levels (SMD = -2.72, 95% CI [-3.37, -2.07], Z = 8.19, P < 0.001). The incidence of adverse events showed no significant difference between the two groups (OR = 0.63, 95% CI [0.28, 1.45], Z = 1.08, P = 0.28).

Conclusion

For pharyngitis patients, the combination of Lanqin Oral Liquid and Western medicine may provide better efficacy compared with Western medicine monotherapy, and its safety profile should be interpreted with caution owing to limited available evidence.

records.title: Efficacy of psychological and behavioral interventions for depressive symptoms in people with epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: Efficacy of psychological and behavioral interventions for depressive symptoms in people with epilepsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Background

Depression is a common and clinically important comorbidity in people with epilepsy and is associated with poorer quality of life, impaired treatment adherence, increased disease burden, and worse clinical outcomes. Psychological and behavioral interventions have been increasingly applied in this population; however, the overall efficacy and consistency of evidence across different intervention categories remain uncertain.

Objective

This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the effects of psychological and behavioral interventions on depressive symptoms in people with epilepsy, with particular attention to cognitive behavioral therapy, mindfulness-based interventions, self-management or collaborative-care programs, and relaxation-based interventions.

Methods

A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, MEDLINE, and Cochrane Library for studies published between January 2005 and May 2026. Randomized controlled trials and controlled clinical studies evaluating eligible interventions for depression-related outcomes in people with epilepsy were included. The primary outcome was depression severity measured using validated rating scales. Standardized mean differences (SMDs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for continuous outcomes. Random-effects models were used to account for clinical and methodological heterogeneity. Risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Cochrane RoB 2 tool and the GRADE framework, respectively.

Results

Twenty-two studies were included in the systematic review, of which 11 contributed data to the quantitative synthesis of continuous depression severity outcomes. Overall, active psychological and behavioral interventions were associated with significantly greater reductions in depressive symptoms compared with treatment as usual or control conditions (SMD = -0.63, 95% CI: -0.90 to -0.36). In subgroup analyses, cognitive behavioral therapy showed a significant beneficial effect (SMD = -0.55, 95% CI: -0.90 to -0.21), as did mindfulness-based interventions (SMD = -0.46, 95% CI: -0.86 to -0.07) and self-management or collaborative-care interventions (SMD = -0.43, 95% CI: -0.74 to -0.12). Progressive muscle relaxation showed a large effect in a single small study (SMD = -1.65), but this finding should be interpreted cautiously because of limited evidence. Most studies were judged as having some concerns regarding risk of bias, mainly due to lack of blinding, reliance on self-reported outcomes, and incomplete outcome reporting. The certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low across intervention categories.

Conclusion

Psychological and behavioral interventions may help reduce depressive symptoms in people with epilepsy. Among the available intervention categories, cognitive behavioral therapy and self-management or collaborative-care interventions showed the most consistent and clinically interpretable evidence. Mindfulness-based interventions may also be beneficial, although the overall certainty of evidence remained low. Findings for progressive muscle relaxation remain preliminary. Further well-designed, adequately powered randomized trials with standardized outcome measures and longer follow-up are needed to confirm these findings.

Systematic review registration

https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261403546, PROSPERO CRD420261403546.

records.title: Deep Learning Image Processing Models in Dermatopathology.

content.title: Deep Learning Image Processing Models in Dermatopathology.
content.abstract: Dermatopathology has rapidly advanced due to the implementation of deep learning models and artificial intelligence (AI). From convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to transformer-based foundation models, these systems are now capable of accurate whole-slide analysis and multimodal integration. This review synthesizes the most recent advents of deep-learning architecture and synthesizes its evolution from first-generation CNNs to hybrid CNN-transformer systems to large-scale foundational models such as Paige's PanDerm AI and Virchow. Herein, we examine performance benchmarks from real-world deployments of major dermatopathology deep learning models (DermAI, PathAssist Derm), as well as emerging next-generation models still under research and development. We assess barriers to clinical workflow adoption such as dataset bias, AI interpretability, and government regulation. Further, we discuss potential future research directions and emphasize the need for diverse, prospectively curated datasets, explainability frameworks for trust in AI, and rigorous compliance to Good Machine-Learning-Practice (GMLP) to achieve safe and scalable deep learning dermatopathology models that can fully integrate into clinical workflows.

records.title: Engineering smart liposomes to combat antimicrobial resistance: from mechanistic design to clinical translation.

content.title: Engineering smart liposomes to combat antimicrobial resistance: from mechanistic design to clinical translation.
content.abstract:
Introduction

Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a critical global health threat, surpassing the pace of discovery and the clinical development of new antimicrobial agents. Therefore, innovative therapeutic strategies are urgently needed to enhance antibiotic efficacy, overcome multidrug-resistant infections, and limit resistance development. Smart liposomal nanoplatforms have emerged as promising tools capable of improving antimicrobial therapy through targeted delivery, enhanced bacterial uptake, biofilm penetration, protection against enzymatic degradation, and controlled drug release.

Areas covered

This review examines recent advances in the rational design of evolved liposomes, including stimuli-responsive and programmable systems, for combating resistant bacterial infections. It discusses their ability to improve pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic profiles, overcome biological barriers, and enable precision antimicrobial delivery. Current translational challenges, including large-scale manufacturing, physicochemical characterization, regulatory requirements, and clinically relevant preclinical models, are critically evaluated. Emerging strategies, such as artificial intelligence-driven formulation optimization, continuous microfluidic manufacturing, multifunctional therapeutic platforms incorporating gene editing, and next-generation antibiotic-adjuvant combination strategies, are also explored.

Expert opinion

Liposomal drug-delivery systems may improve the exposure, distribution, and intracellular or local delivery of antimicrobial agents, but improved delivery should not be equated with reversal of bacterial resistance. Successful clinical translation will depend on formulation- and infection-specific evidence, clinically relevant preclinical models, controlled and scalable manufacturing, and appropriate regulatory frameworks, while artificial intelligence, digital-twin, and precision-medicine approaches are best viewed as decision-support tools that complement experimental and clinical validation.

records.title: Biological Variability and Biomedical Innovation in Personalized Orthodontics: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis.

content.title: Biological Variability and Biomedical Innovation in Personalized Orthodontics: A Systematic Review with Narrative Synthesis.
content.abstract: Background/Objectives: Orthodontic treatment response varies considerably among patients because mechanical loading interacts with individual biological, anatomical, systemic, and behavioral characteristics. Advances in mechanobiology, molecular biomarkers, omics technologies, and artificial intelligence (AI) may support a more personalized approach to treatment. This systematic review (SR) aimed to evaluate human clinical evidence concerning these domains and their potential contribution to predicting orthodontic response, improving clinical decision-making, and reducing adverse effects. Methods: A systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science was conducted through June 2026. Primary studies involving human participants and addressing orthodontic tooth movement (OTM), biological variability, biomarkers, genomics, epigenetics, multi-omics, or AI-supported orthodontics were selected according to predefined eligibility criteria. The review was conducted and reported in accordance with Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020, and heterogeneous evidence was synthesized narratively across four predefined domains. The review protocol was registered in the International Prospective Register of Systematic Reviews (PROSPERO; registration number CRD420261486348). Risk of bias was assessed using design-appropriate instruments. Certainty of evidence was assessed at the outcome level using GRADE principles adapted to narrative synthesis. Results: The search identified 1051 records, of which 14 primary human studies were included. The clinical evidence comprised randomized trials, longitudinal and cross-sectional biomarker studies, genetic association studies, and a case report. Molecular and multi-omics studies identified candidate markers of biological response and patient phenotype. The included computational studies examined genetic association rules, gingival-enlargement classification, and AI-assisted root-resorption measurement; none demonstrated AI-guided selection of orthodontic forces. However, small samples, methodological heterogeneity, limited adjustment for confounding, and lack of external validation restricted clinical translation. Certainty of evidence supporting clinical personalization applications was predominantly very low. Conclusions: Personalized orthodontics should remain grounded in comprehensive diagnosis, biologically compatible mechanics, and individualized monitoring. Molecular and computational tools may complement clinical assessment, but routine implementation requires standardized protocols, multicenter validation, and prospective evidence of patient-relevant benefit.

records.title: Non-invasive biomarkers in assisted reproductive technologies, current evidence, clinical utility and future perspectives.

content.title: Non-invasive biomarkers in assisted reproductive technologies, current evidence, clinical utility and future perspectives.
content.abstract: Although assisted reproductive technologies have significantly advanced the treatment of infertility, overall success rates remain limited by the lack of accurate and safe tools for assessing reproductive potential. Conventional embryo selection and endometrial evaluation rely largely on morphological and non-functional criteria, which provide only indirect insight into the underlying biological competence of the embryo oocyte and uterine environment. In this context the development of non-invasive biomarkers has emerged as a critical objective in modern reproductive medicine. This review discusses current evidence on non-invasive biomarkers in in vitro fertilization and assisted reproductive technologies with emphasis on embryo derived follicular fluid and endometrial indicators. Advances in time lapse imaging analysis of spent embryo culture media follicular fluid profiling and uterine fluid assessment are discussed in relation to their biological significance and association with clinical outcomes. The role of metabolomic proteomic transcriptomic and genetic signals is examined alongside emerging applications of artificial intelligence for data integration and outcome prediction. While numerous non-invasive biomarkers demonstrate promising associations with embryo viability implantation potential and surrogate pregnancy outcomes, with limited evidence in live birth rates, their clinical translation is constrained by methodological heterogeneity, limited validation, and challenges in standardization. Integrative multi parameter approaches rather than single biomarker strategies appear most likely to enhance predictive accuracy. Continued efforts toward data harmonization, large scale validation, and clinically oriented model development are essential for the successful incorporation of non-invasive biomarkers into routine IVF practice. Curated databases and relevant AI applications may facilitate and help progress non-invasive biomarkers in ART.

records.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Implementation in Maternal and Child Health: A Scoping Review.

content.title: Artificial Intelligence (AI) Implementation in Maternal and Child Health: A Scoping Review.
content.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has increasingly been applied in maternal and child health. However, current evidence remains largely focused on model development, while reports on real-world clinical implementation are limited. This scoping review aimed to map the implementation of AI in maternal and child health settings and summarize reported outcomes. This scoping review followed the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR) guideline. Searches were conducted in PubMed and Scopus using Boolean operators combining terms related to artificial intelligence, maternal and child health, and implementation. Studies published in English between 2021 and 2026 were included if they reported clinical or community-based implementation of AI involving real patients or healthcare providers within an ongoing care pathway. Studies focused solely on AI model development or technical validation, reviews, conference abstracts, and editorials were excluded. Of 191 records identified, 156 were screened after duplicate removal, 64 full-text reports were assessed, and seven studies met all inclusion criteria. Identified AI applications were grouped into three themes: maternal support and community-based interventions, neonatal and pediatric monitoring, and screening and diagnostic support. Included studies reported promising outcomes, including improved monitoring accuracy, maternal engagement, and image quality standardization in low-resource settings. However, the seven included studies were highly heterogeneous, and most remained limited to feasibility studies or early-stage implementations. Current evidence suggests AI holds promise as an assistive tool in maternal and child healthcare. However, given the limited number and heterogeneity of included studies, this evidence should be interpreted as preliminary. Organizational, regulatory, financial, and workforce-related barriers, along with ethical considerations such as data privacy and algorithmic bias, remain to be addressed. Further large-scale, long-term implementation studies are needed to evaluate the integration and sustainability of AI in routine maternal and child healthcare practice.

records.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Preoperative Planning in Surgery: A Narrative Review.

content.title: Use of Artificial Intelligence in Preoperative Planning in Surgery: A Narrative Review.
content.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into preoperative planning for surgery has shown significant potential for enhancing surgical outcomes. AI technologies, such as machine learning (ML), deep learning, three-dimensional (3D) modeling, and predictive analytics, are increasingly being used to improve the accuracy of surgical planning, risk stratification, and patient outcomes. The aim of this narrative review was primarily to evaluate the applications, effectiveness, and limitations of AI in preoperative surgical planning. This review synthesized findings from recent studies published between 2020 and 2025, focusing on the use of AI in preoperative planning across surgical specialties, with particular attention to well-documented examples from plastic and reconstructive surgery. AI technologies, including ML algorithms, 3D modeling, and predictive analytics, have shown promise in potentially improving surgical precision, reducing complications, and enhancing patient satisfaction across multiple surgical procedures. However, challenges related to data heterogeneity, publication bias, and the limited number of large-scale prospective multicenter clinical studies remain significant barriers to its broader implementation. AI can potentially support preoperative planning in surgery by augmenting surgical decision-making and contributing to improved clinical outcomes. Integrating AI with emerging technologies, such as 3D printing and virtual reality, could further expand its applications in surgical planning and patient care.

records.title: The efficacy and safety of danuglipron and orforglipron in patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.

content.title: The efficacy and safety of danuglipron and orforglipron in patients with type 2 diabetes and obesity: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
content.abstract:
Objective

This study assesses the efficacy and safety of the novel oral small molecule glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) danuglipron and orforglipron in the treatment of type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and obesity through systematic review and meta-analysis.

Methods

Electronic databases (PubMed, Web of Science, Cochrane Library and Embase) were systematically searched up to 20 May 2025 to include randomised controlled trials evaluating danuglipron/orforglipron in patients with T2DM and/or obesity. Changes in glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting plasma insulin (FPI), weight and body mass index (BMI) compared with baseline post-treatment were evaluated using random-/fixed-effects models, alongside safety outcomes.

Results

Eight studies with low bias risk involving 1,454 participants were analysed. Meta-analysis results demonstrated that danuglipron significantly decreased HbA1c (mean difference [MD]: -0.90; 95% CI: -1.06, -0.74), FPG (MD: -24.66; 95% CI: -30.45, -18.86) and weight (MD: -2.17; 95% CI: -3.10, -1.23) and improved FPI (MD: 2.94; 95% CI: 1.50, 4.38). Orforglipron also showed significant positive effects on HbA1c (MD: -1.02; 95% CI: -1.18, -0.86), FPG (MD: -26.91; 95% CI: -31.05, -22.78), weight (MD: -6.28; 95% CI: -8.45, -4.11) and BMI (MD: -2.64; 95% CI: -3.38, -1.89). However, both danuglipron and orforglipron were associated with the occurrence of treatment-related adverse events and gastrointestinal adverse events (AEs).

Conclusion

The oral GLP-1 RAs danuglipron and orforglipron are capable of improving blood glucose levels and reducing weight; however, they also pose an increased risk of gastrointestinal AEs. Further longitudinal studies are warranted to gain a deeper understanding of their efficacy, safety and tolerability.

records.title: Wastewater Membrane Bioreactors: A Comprehensive Review of Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Digital Twin Applications.

content.title: Wastewater Membrane Bioreactors: A Comprehensive Review of Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Digital Twin Applications.
content.abstract: Wastewater membrane bioreactors (MBRs) have become an important advanced treatment technology due to their ability to produce high-quality effluent suitable for discharge and water reuse. However, their broader and more sustainable application remains constrained by membrane fouling, elevated energy demand, and the operational complexity of coupled biological and membrane separation processes. This comprehensive review critically evaluates the growing application of machine learning (ML), explainable artificial intelligence (XAI), and digital twin (DT) technologies in MBR systems. Published studies on fouling prediction, energy optimization, effluent quality estimation, and intelligent operational support are critically evaluated, with explicit attention to model performance, dataset limitations, and generalizability. The reviewed literature shows that ML models, particularly ensemble methods, support vector machines, and deep learning approaches, have demonstrated strong potential for predicting major MBR performance indicators, including transmembrane pressure, permeate flux, fouling resistance, and selected effluent-quality variables. In parallel, XAI methods such as SHAP, LIME, and Anchors are increasingly being used to enhance model transparency and to reveal the dominant factors controlling process performance. Digital twin frameworks further extend this potential by enabling the integration of mechanistic understanding, online sensor data, data-driven prediction, and interpretable decision support within real-time operational platforms. Nevertheless, several barriers continue to hinder practical implementation, including the limited number of full-scale studies, the scarcity of openly accessible and standardized datasets, insufficient consideration of uncertainty and model drift, and the early-stage maturity of DT deployment in operational plants. The evidence reviewed suggests that integrating ML, XAI, and DT can substantially improve the reliability, interpretability, and operational efficiency of MBR systems. Future research should therefore focus on full-scale validation, the development of benchmark datasets, uncertainty-aware modeling, and practical deployment strategies for interpretable intelligent MBR management.

records.title: The potential effect of whey protein supplementation in post-bariatric surgery patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.

content.title: The potential effect of whey protein supplementation in post-bariatric surgery patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
content.abstract:
Background
